title: model configuration entities properties and keys
concepts: EF Core builds an IModel from CLR types, conventions, attributes, and fluent configuration. The model is a mapping contract; it is not the database schema itself.

Entity types represent tracked identity-bearing rows; keyless entity types are query shapes without change-tracking identity. Complex/value objects and owned entities have different identity and mapping semantics.
Property mapping controls column names, types, nullability, conversion, generated values, and field access. A CLR property type does not automatically guarantee identical database semantics.

Primary keys identify entities; alternate keys participate in relationships, while unique indexes enforce uniqueness without necessarily creating EF key identity. Provider-specific options must be labeled.
Fluent configuration is explicit and generally takes precedence over conventions and attributes; model validation and migrations reveal incompatible or ambiguous mappings.

items: EF Core 10 added complex types mapped to JSON with ToJson. EF Core 11.0.0 is released and adds complex types/JSON columns with TPT/TPC, complex types in Cosmos, chained nested property configuration, complex collections, and keys/indexes on nested complex-type paths (including applicable JSON paths). Do not describe these shipped EF Core 11 capabilities as preview-only.
